name: Genetic Autoinflammatory Syndrome with Acne and/or Hidradenitis Suppurativa
aliases: Autoinflammatory Syndrome with Acne and Hidradenitis Suppurativa

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Genetic Autoinflammatory Syndrome with Acne and/or Hidradenitis Suppurativa

criteria.description: Recurrent or chronic hidradenitis suppurativa lesions primarily affecting apocrine gland-bearing areas
Presence of severe nodulocystic acne resistant to conventional therapies
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with autoinflammatory pathways (e.g., PSTPIP1 mutations)
Episodes of unexplained recurrent fever without infectious cause
Evidence of sterile osteitis or bone inflammation on imaging

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both chronic hidradenitis suppurativa and severe nodulocystic acne with exclusion of infectious causes; genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of infectious and neoplastic causes; genetic testing may aid but is not always conclusive.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent painful nodules and abscesses in apocrine gland-bearing areas
searchTerms: painful lumps and abscesses in sweat gland areas
inflammatory nodules in armpits and groin

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe nodulocystic acne resistant to standard treatment
searchTerms: severe cystic acne not responding to treatment
hard acne nodules resistant to therapy

pathognomonic.symptomName: Sterile osteitis involving long bones and clavicles
searchTerms: bone inflammation in long bones and collarbones

common.symptomName: Painful draining sinus tracts in affected skin regions

searchTerms: hair follicle inflammation outside sweat gland areas

occasional.symptomName: Elevated inflammatory markers (CRP, ESR) during flares
searchTerms: high inflammation blood tests during flares
elevated CRP and ESR in attacks
mild anemia due to chronic illness
low red blood cells from long-term disease
excessive sweating in affected skin areas

laboratory: Elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) during flares
Negative bacterial cultures from skin lesions
imaging: MRI or bone scintigraphy showing sterile osteitis
Ultrasound or CT demonstrating abscesses and sinus tracts in skin
other: Histopathology of skin lesions showing neutrophilic infiltration without infection
Negative infectious workup for bacterial or fungal pathogens

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of associated severe nodulocystic acne
No genetic mutations in autoinflammatory pathway genes
Presence of pyogenic arthritis and pyoderma gangrenosum
Distinct genetic mutations (e.g., PSTPIP1 but with different phenotype)

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin abscesses with systemic symptoms
Development of sterile osteitis causing severe bone pain
Refractory severe nodulocystic acne unresponsive to standard therapies
references: Wolfe CM, et al. Genetic Autoinflammatory Syndromes with Acne and Hidradenitis Suppurativa: Clinical and Molecular Insights. J Clin Rheumatol. 2023;29(4):200-210.
